issues.problem: The ad promises a specific, quantified outcome (up to 15% body weight loss) with clinician-led care, but the page headline drops the number and the clinician framing, so ad-clickers lose continuity and may doubt the claim.

## Headline

**Don't ship.** The CI on relative lift includes zero at the planned sample, so keep the current start page and treat the result as a near-miss worth one redesigned follow-up, not a rollout.
Hypothesis: showing the clinician review step and expected timing on the start page lifts assessment completion for first-time paid social visitors.
Primary metric: completion rate (started → submitted); MDE 10% relative; ship if the 95% CI on relative lift excludes zero and the estimate is ≥10%, don't ship if the CI includes zero at the planned sample.

## What actually ran

- **Test window:** 2026-10-22 to 2026-11-05 (14 days), 50/50 split, Control vs Variant A.
- **Sample:** Control 49,912; Variant A 49,760. Plan was 49,800 per arm, so the smallest arm is 40 short of plan (0.1%). Treated as planned sample reached.
- **Sample ratio check:** passed (χ² = 0.232, p = 0.6302).
- **Baseline:** 3.2% completion. Power was set at 80% for a 10% relative MDE, α 5%.
- **Deviations:**
  - Tracking gap of about 4 hours on day 3, affecting both arms. Impact on the result is not quantified. [MISSING: number of starts or completions lost in the gap]
  - Paid social spend rose 30% from day 9, with the same split across arms. This changes traffic mix mid-test, which may affect how far the result generalises. [MISSING: completion rate by arm before and after day 9]
- **Pre-registered segments:** mobile vs desktop; paid social vs organic. [MISSING: paid social vs organic results]

## Results

**Primary: completion rate.**
+6.9% relative (95% CI −0.28% to +14.08%); p = 0.0514 (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0514, one comparison).
Control 3.2% (1,597 of 49,912) vs Variant A 3.42% (1,702 of 49,760), an absolute lift of +0.221 pts.
The interval includes zero and the point estimate is below the 10% MDE. The interval does extend above 10%, so a true effect at or above the MDE cannot be ruled out.

**Guardrails.**
- Support contacts per start: Control 1.8%, Variant A 1.9%. **Passed.** [MISSING: CI on the difference]
- Refund rate within 14 days: Control 2.4%, Variant A 2.3%. **Passed.** [MISSING: CI on the difference]

**Pre-registered segments.**
- Mobile: +9.1% relative (95% CI −1.2% to +19.4%). Includes zero.
- Desktop: +3.0% relative (95% CI −8.5% to +14.5%). Includes zero.
- Paid social vs organic: [MISSING: results for both segments]

Neither segment excludes zero, and the segment intervals are wider than the overall interval.

**Annualised value.**
Annualised value of the lift: £0 to £0 is not supported; the range from the computed interval is **−£5,060 at the CI low to +£256,757 at the CI high**. The range spans a small annual loss to a substantial gain, so no central value is reliable enough to plan against. [MISSING: annualisation assumptions (volume, value per completion)]

### Exploratory (not pre-registered)

Nothing outside the pre-registered segments was analysed, and none of the following is evidence. Future hypotheses only:
- The mobile point estimate (+9.1%) is larger than desktop (+3.0%). Worth testing a mobile-specific version of the start page, but the segment intervals overlap heavily and include zero.
- The mid-test paid social spend increase may have shifted the audience toward colder, less informed visitors, who could respond differently to the explainer. This would need a pre/post-day-9 cut, planned in advance.

## Interpretation

This is a null at the planned sample, not a failed test. The estimate is positive (+6.9%) and the interval reaches +14.08%, so a worthwhile effect is plausible, but the data do not distinguish it from no effect (p = 0.0514 is just above the 5% threshold). The decision rule says don't ship when the CI includes zero at the planned sample, and we are applying it as written.

The verdict follows the decision rule; there is no deviation.

Risks to the read: the day 3 tracking gap hit both arms equally so it is unlikely to bias the comparison, but it is unquantified. The 30% spend increase from day 9 changed the traffic mix for both arms, which limits how confidently the result transfers to steady-state paid social traffic. Guardrails were stable, so the variant does no visible harm to support load or refunds; this lowers the cost of a follow-up test but does not justify shipping.

## Decision and next steps

- **Don't ship Variant A.** Keep the current start page.
- Decide whether to run one follow-up. The upside case (CI high end, around £256,757 a year) is large relative to the downside (−£5,060), so a sharper second test is reasonable if the team has capacity. Owner and date: [MISSING].
- If iterating, prioritise a mobile-first version of the start page, as a new pre-registered hypothesis rather than a post-hoc segment win.
- Before any rerun, quantify the day 3 tracking gap and confirm the paid social spend change is held constant or logged as a stratification variable.
- Fill the missing paid social vs organic cut from the original pre-registration so the experiment record is complete.

## Learnings to log

- First-time paid social visitors showed a small, unconfirmed lean toward completing when told what happens after the quiz; the effect is not distinguishable from zero. [surface: assessment] [principle: set expectations] [segment: paid social] [outcome: flat]
- Mobile visitors leaned positive (+9.1%) but the interval includes zero, so the mobile-first hypothesis remains open. [surface: assessment] [principle: progressive disclosure] [segment: mobile] [outcome: flat]
- Explaining the clinician review step did not change support contacts or refunds, so uncertainty about what happens next is not a visible driver of support demand. [surface: assessment] [principle: set expectations] [segment: all visitors] [outcome: flat]

## Appendix

- **Raw counts:** Control 1,597 completions of 49,912 starts; Variant A 1,702 of 49,760.
- **Rates:** Control 3.2%; Variant A 3.42%; absolute lift +0.221 pts; relative lift +6.9%.
- **Primary stats:** 95% CI on relative lift −0.28% to +14.08%; p = 0.0514; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0514 (single comparison, no other arms).
- **SRM:** χ² = 0.232, p = 0.6302, no mismatch.
- **Power and design:** MDE 10% relative; planned 49,800 per arm; smallest arm 49,760; power 80%; α 5%; 14 days.
- **Annualised value:** −£5,060 (CI low) to +£256,757 (CI high). [MISSING: central estimate and assumptions]
- **Data note:** Sample test (synthetic data).

# A/B Test Brief: Single Price Breakdown Next to Primary CTA

## Hypothesis

We believe that showing a single price breakdown next to the primary CTA for new paid-traffic visitors will increase assessment starts and reduce month-2 cancellations.

The price breakdown contains four elements: intro price, what the price becomes after month one, total commitment, and a "no other fees" line.

**Evidence behind the belief:**
- Users scroll to the pricing section repeatedly before deciding.
- Users ask in chat whether the price is final.
- Users cancel after an unnoticed price rise.

**We will know this is true when** assessment start rate moves by at least +8% relative, with 30-day cancellation rate unchanged or lower.

Note: the pre-registered MDE is 10% relative (see Sample size), which is stricter than the +8% in the hypothesis. The decision rule uses 10%. An observed lift between 8% and 10% is not powered to be detected and is treated as inconclusive below.

## Change

**Control:** Current landing page, pricing section and checkout summary, with no consolidated price breakdown beside the primary CTA.

**Variant:** A single price breakdown block placed adjacent to the primary CTA on the landing page, repeated in the pricing section and the checkout summary. Contents, in this order:
1. Intro price
2. Price after month one
3. Total commitment
4. "No other fees" line

**Scope:**
- Surface: landing page, pricing section, checkout summary.
- Audience: new visitors arriving via paid traffic only. Returning visitors and non-paid sources are excluded.
- Allocation: 50/50, randomised at visitor level, persistent across sessions.
- Exact copy and prices: [TO CONFIRM]. Legal/compliance review of the "no other fees" claim: [TO CONFIRM].

## Primary metric

**Landing page to assessment start rate:** unique visitors who start an assessment divided by unique visitors who land on the page, per arm.

- Baseline: 3.20%
- Unit: visitor
- Attribution window: [TO CONFIRM] (e.g. same session or 7 days from first exposure)
- Definition of "assessment start": [TO CONFIRM] (first question displayed vs first answer submitted)

## Guardrail metrics

| Metric | Definition | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| 30-day cancellation rate | Share of converted customers in each arm who cancel within 30 days of purchase | Must be unchanged or lower. Breach = variant higher than control with the 95% CI lower bound above 0 |

- Baseline 30-day cancellation rate: [TO CONFIRM]
- Non-inferiority margin for "unchanged": [TO CONFIRM]
- The 30-day cancellation read matures only after the last enrolled purchaser has had 30 days. It is read at the end of the maturation window, not during the enrolment run.
- Additional operational guardrails (checkout completion rate, chat contacts about price, page error rate): [TO CONFIRM]

## Pre-specified success criteria and decision rule

**MDE: 10% relative on assessment start rate** (3.20% to 3.52% absolute, +0.32 pp).

Evaluated once, at planned sample, on the 95% confidence interval of the relative lift, with the guardrail read after the cancellation maturation window.

| Outcome | Decision |
|---|---|
| **CI includes zero** | No evidence of effect. Do not ship. Retain control. Log as inconclusive; any follow-up test needs a new brief. |
| **CI excludes zero but lower bound/point estimate misses the 10% MDE** | Effect is real but below the commercial threshold. Do not ship on this evidence. Review with owner whether the lift justifies the maintenance cost; default is to retain control. |
| **CI clears the MDE (lower bound ≥ +10% relative) and cancellation guardrail holds** | Ship variant to 100% of paid-traffic new visitors. |
| **CI clears the MDE but cancellation guardrail breached** | Do not ship. Investigate the cancellation driver before any rollout. |

A point estimate above 10% with a CI that still includes values below 10% falls under the second row.

## Pre-registered segments

At most three. Segment results are exploratory and cannot override the primary decision rule.

1. **Device (mobile vs desktop).** The CTA and breakdown share limited space on mobile, so layout effects may differ.
2. **Paid channel (search vs social) [channel split TO CONFIRM].** Intent differs by channel, and price sensitivity is likely to differ with it.
3. **Intro-price offer tier [TO CONFIRM].** The gap between intro price and post-month-one price varies by offer, so the disclosure effect should scale with it.

No other cuts will be reported as findings.

## Sample size and run time

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Baseline conversion | 3.20% |
| MDE | 10% relative |
| Power | 80% |
| Alpha | 5% |
| Arms | 2 |
| Visitors per arm | 49,777 |
| Total visitors | 99,554 |
| Eligible traffic | 4,000 visitors/day |
| Calculated duration | 25 days |
| **Planned run time** | **28 days** (rounded up to whole weeks; exceeds the 14-day minimum) |

- At 4,000 visitors/day over 28 days, expected enrolment is 112,000 visitors, above the 99,554 required.
- The sample is powered for the primary metric only. The cancellation guardrail is not powered at this sample and relies on the maturation window plus the non-inferiority margin [TO CONFIRM].
- Cancellation maturation: purchasers enrolled on the last day need 30 further days. Final guardrail read is therefore at about day 58.
- Daily traffic assumption of 4,000 should be validated against the last 4 weeks of paid traffic: [TO CONFIRM].

## Stop rule

- **No peeking before the planned sample** is reached on the primary metric. No interim looks, dashboards for decision purposes, or early calls.
- **Earliest valid read:** end of day 28, once at least 49,777 visitors per arm are enrolled (whichever is later).
- **Only exception:** a guardrail breach. If the variant's cancellation rate (or any operational guardrail defined as [TO CONFIRM]) breaches its pre-set threshold, the test may be stopped early and the variant rolled back. Because the 30-day cancellation read matures slowly, an early guardrail check is limited to operational signals available sooner (checkout errors, price-related chat contacts) [TO CONFIRM thresholds].
- A stop for guardrail breach is recorded as a failed test, not as evidence of effect on the primary metric.
- Sample ratio mismatch check (expected 50/50, threshold p < 0.001) is run as a data-quality check, not a performance peek. If it fails, the test is invalid and restarts after the cause is fixed.

## Risks and dependencies

- **Legal/compliance:** "No other fees" is a factual claim and must be accurate for all plans and regions. [TO CONFIRM] sign-off.
- **Tracking:** assessment start event and purchase-to-cancellation linkage must be verified in both arms before launch. [TO CONFIRM]
- **Price changes mid-test:** any change to intro price or post-month-one price during the run invalidates the test. Pricing freeze required for the run plus maturation window.
- **Concurrent experiments and paid-media changes:** campaign mix shifts, new creatives or other landing page tests overlapping with this audience would confound results. [TO CONFIRM] experiment calendar.
- **Novelty/seasonality:** 28 days covers four full weekly cycles; promotional periods inside the window are [TO CONFIRM].
- **Metric tension:** disclosure could lower start rate by deterring price-sensitive users. This is a valid outcome, and the decision rule treats it as a no-ship.
- **Engineering:** variant build and QA across the three surfaces, including mobile layout. Effort and launch date [TO CONFIRM].
- **Cancellation readout lag:** final decision is gated on day ~58. Stakeholders must accept this delay.

value.firstTest: Run the pricing transparency block first: it is a corroborated item (research and page audit) with the highest severity (5) and the strongest combined confidence, and it targets the hesitation and hidden-charge cancellations that directly gate purchase. If the long assessment is judged to be blocking more purchases than price uncertainty, the single-source assessment-friction fix is the alternative, but it carries more build effort and lacks page-side corroboration.

ed45e58861b4aa0e1bb22e96cf16e829f940d546.text: None of these three experiments has produced a win: all 3 of 3 came back flat, every one of them on the assessment surface. The "set expectations" principle has been tried 2 times and went flat both times, once on paid social visitors and once on all visitors, while "progressive disclosure" has been tried once, on mobile, and also went flat, with a +9.1% lean whose interval includes zero. Nothing has been tested on any surface other than the assessment, and the only segments covered are paid social, mobile, and all visitors, so there are no wins on any segment, surface, or principle. The biggest gap is that every test so far sits on a single surface, leaving the rest of the funnel, and any segment beyond paid social and mobile, entirely unexamined.

7396c9eb46976ae03166c3276f237504abe1eaad.text:
Start with the mobile hero fix, which has the highest risk score (42) and is the cheapest to build, so it tests our shakiest assumption for almost no effort. Second, run the comparison table move (35), which is equally cheap but sits on a different section of the landing page; to avoid overlap on the same page, I'd stagger it or restrict it to comparison-shopping traffic, and I'd rather not run it concurrently with the hero test if both feed the same start-rate metric. Third, run the testimonials swap (30, tied with plan management, but easier), which tests unrelatable proof for 35+ visitors, only after the earlier landing-page tests finish.

I deferred the pricing, clinical-review, checkout-confirmation and assessment-flow tests because their evidence is stronger and risk scores are lower. Plan management ties at 30 but is a harder build and doesn't share the landing page.

rules.reason: Names the prescription-only medicine Wegovy together with a benefit, which is prohibited public advertising under HWG §10 and is a classic Abmahnung trigger.
'Up to 15% of body weight' is an unsubstantiated numerical efficacy claim with no population, period or evidence basis stated.
Presents a weight-loss outcome of a medicine as an expected result; results vary and no certainty or efficacy promise is permitted (HWG §11).
'Get your prescription today' and 'medication delivered to your door' presume the clinician's decision; a prescription is not assured.
'Doctor recommended' is a health-professional endorsement of a medicine, prohibited under HWG §11.
Overall impression is that medication is obtainable on request, while eligibility, clinician decision and conditions are omitted.

rules.reason: 'Approbierte Ärztin' is a factual claim; every assessing clinician must hold a German licence (Approbation) or equivalent recognised qualification, evidenced before publication.
Acceptable because 'was in Ihrem Fall sinnvoll ist' leaves the decision open; must not drift toward promising a medicine.
'Jetzt' is a mild urgency cue; must not suggest a time-limited offer.

variants.rewrite: Ärztliche Begleitung beim Abnehmen. Online, persönlich. | Eine Ärztin prüft Ihre Situation und bespricht mit Ihnen, was in Ihrem Fall sinnvoll ist. | Einschätzung beginnen
variants.disclosure: Ob und welche Behandlung angezeigt ist, entscheidet ausschließlich die Ärztin bzw. der Arzt nach individueller Prüfung. Ergebnisse sind individuell verschieden. Ärztliche Qualifikation und Kosten (inkl. MwSt.) im Impressum/auf der Seite ausgewiesen.

value.why: Variant B is the only one that is clear as written and it tests the hypothesis most directly by showing who assesses you and what happens next in three concrete steps, with no medicine named and no outcome implied.

aesthetic.evidence: No screenshots attached; judged from structure only. 9 images and a clean heading outline (h1 'Take control of your weight' then 5 h2s) suggest a polished template, but 13 nav links and 4 competing CTAs undermine perceived usability.
aesthetic.fix: Reduce the visual noise in the first viewport (cut nav to 4 items, one CTA) and measure assessment-start rate and bounce rate on mobile.

choice.evidence: The 'Start now' section presents 16 options ('Lose 5kg' through 'Lose 80kg') as a single choice, plus 3 hero CTAs ('Start your free assessment', 'Learn more', 'See pricing') and 13 nav links.
choice.fix: Replace the 16 goal buttons with a slider or 3 bands (under 10kg / 10-25kg / 25kg+) and cut hero CTAs to one; measure assessment-start click-through and time-to-first-click.

chunking.evidence: Headings split the page into sensible sections (How it works, Start now, From £149/month, FAQs), but the 'How it works' block is one dense paragraph covering steps, requirements, timing and refund policy.
chunking.fix: Convert 'How it works' into a 3-step numbered list with a separate 'What you'll need' line (ID, recent weight); measure scroll depth to the CTA and assessment starts.

bias.evidence: 'Trusted by 50,000+ members' leverages social proof and 'From £149/month' anchors price, but the heading has no supporting reviews, ratings or source, and the 'Lose 80kg' options may trigger unrealistic expectations or optimism bias.
bias.fix: Attach a verifiable proof element (rating with review count or named testimonial) next to the 50,000+ claim; measure CTA click-through and trust-related drop-off.

load.evidence: Only 199 words, yet 13 nav links, 4 CTAs, 16 weight options and 8 form fields compete for attention; the how-it-works paragraph bundles medical history, ID, timing and charging rules.
load.fix: Strip nav to logo + Log in + CTA on mobile, and reduce the hero to one headline, one line of support and one CTA; measure assessment-start rate and time-to-first-interaction.

doherty.evidence: Response timing cannot be judged from static content; only 9 scripts and 3KB of HTML are visible, with no evidence of latency.
doherty.fix: Instrument INP and step-transition time on the 'Continue' click and test whether a sub-400ms transition improves quiz step completion rate.

fitts.evidence: No screenshots attached; judged from structure only. The 'Start assessment' nav link is the 13th item in a crowded bar, and on mobile the 16 'Lose Xkg' options plus 'Continue' risk small, tightly packed tap targets.
fitts.fix: Make the hero CTA full-width with at least 48px height and sticky at the bottom on mobile; measure mis-tap rate and CTA click-through.

flow.evidence: The path 'Start your free assessment' -> weight goal -> 'Continue' is straightforward, but the 'Learn more' and 'See pricing' CTAs and an 8-field form interrupt momentum with exits.
flow.fix: Move the assessment into a one-question-per-screen flow without nav links; measure completion rate and step-to-step drop-off.

goal.evidence: There is no progress indicator or sense of advancement; the text mentions a 10 to 15 minute assessment but shows no steps, and 'Continue' gives no sense of how many steps remain.
goal.fix: Add a 'Step 1 of 5' progress bar with pre-filled first step (selected goal) and measure assessment completion rate.

region.evidence: No screenshots attached; judged from structure only. Headings imply distinct sections, but there is no evidence of cards or bordered containers separating 'Start now' options from pricing and FAQ.
region.fix: Wrap the goal selector and CTA in a single bordered card distinct from the surrounding content; measure assessment-start rate.

proximity.evidence: No screenshots attached; judged from structure only. The three hero CTAs ('Start your free assessment', 'Learn more', 'See pricing') sit together with equal grouping, implying equal importance, and the 16 'Lose Xkg' labels run together without grouping.
proximity.fix: Group the primary CTA with its reassurance line ('Free, 10-15 minutes') and separate secondary links with spacing; measure primary CTA click share.

pragnanz.evidence: The page structure is conventional (hero, proof, how it works, start, pricing, FAQ), but the 16-option list and 13-link nav turn simple sections into cluttered ones.
pragnanz.fix: Simplify the first viewport to headline, one sentence, one CTA and one proof line; measure bounce rate and CTA click-through.

similarity.evidence: 'Start assessment', 'Start your free assessment', 'Continue', 'Learn more' and 'View plans' are presumably styled as similar buttons with near-identical wording, so the main action does not stand apart from other actions.
similarity.fix: Use one label ('Start free assessment') and one filled style, with secondary actions as text links; measure primary CTA click share.

connected.evidence: No screenshots attached; judged from structure only. Nothing indicates the 'How it works' steps are visually linked in sequence; the steps appear as running prose.
connected.fix: Add a vertical connector line linking numbered steps 1-3 and ending in the CTA; measure scroll-to-CTA and click-through.

mental.evidence: The labels follow familiar telehealth patterns: 'Take the quiz. A clinician reviews your answers. If appropriate, treatment is delivered to your door', and 'From £149/month' with 'pause or cancel at any time'.
mental.fix: Keep the familiar sequence but add 'Free assessment' near the CTA to confirm the expected quiz-first pattern; measure assessment-start rate.

miller.evidence: The page presents 16 weight options and 13 nav links, exceeding 7±2 items, and the how-it-works text lists five assessment topics plus ID and weight requirements in one paragraph.
miller.fix: Cap nav to 4 items and weight choices to 3-5 bands; measure time-to-first-click and assessment-start rate.

occam.evidence: The core hypothesis (take quiz, get reviewed, get treatment) is simple, but the page layers on a goal picker, a pricing teaser, FAQs and several CTAs before the quiz.
occam.fix: Remove the standalone 'Start now' goal picker and make the first quiz step the goal question; measure assessment-start and completion rates.

active.evidence: Users will tap straight into the quiz, but the how-it-works section is one long paragraph that mobile users will skip, burying requirements like 'photo ID and a recent weight'.
active.fix: Surface the 'You'll need: photo ID and recent weight' in a short checklist just before the CTA; measure mid-assessment abandonment.

pareto.evidence: A few elements (headline, 'Start your free assessment', 'Trusted by 50,000+ members', pricing from £149/month) drive the decision, while 13 nav links, a blog link and 16 weight options add little.
pareto.fix: Prune secondary nav links (Blog, About, Science, Contact) from the mobile header into the footer; measure share of sessions reaching the assessment.

parkinson.evidence: The page sets a time expectation: 'Most people complete the assessment in 10 to 15 minutes and hear back within 24 hours'.
parkinson.fix: Move the '10-15 minutes' time promise onto the CTA as microcopy and test completion time and rate.

peakend.evidence: The end of the page is FAQs and footer links (Privacy, Terms, Contact) rather than a final CTA, and 'If you don't qualify we'll explain why' hints at a negative end state with no described softener.
peakend.fix: Add a closing CTA after FAQs ('Start your free assessment') and design a helpful not-eligible outcome; measure post-assessment satisfaction and return rate.

postel.evidence: The form has 8 fields and requires 'photo ID and a recent weight', yet no mention of flexible input (units kg/st, upload alternatives) appears on the page.
postel.fix: Accept kg, st/lb and cm/ft-in with auto-conversion and allow ID upload later; measure field error rate and form completion.

attention.evidence: Four CTAs ('Start assessment', 'Start your free assessment', 'Learn more', 'Continue') and 13 nav links split attention in the first viewport on mobile.
attention.fix: Hide nav behind a menu and keep a single high-contrast CTA above the fold; measure primary CTA click-through.

tesler.evidence: Medical intake complexity (medical history, medications, ID, weight) is inherent, and the page acknowledges it: 'We'll ask about your medical history, current medications, weight history, goals and lifestyle'.
tesler.fix: Keep required medical questions but pre-fill or defer ID upload to after eligibility; measure assessment completion rate.

restorff.evidence: With 'Start assessment', 'Start your free assessment', 'Learn more' and 'View plans' plus 16 similar 'Lose Xkg' options, no single element is likely to stand out.
restorff.fix: Give the hero CTA a unique high-contrast fill that no other element uses; measure primary CTA click share.

working.evidence: The how-it-works text asks users to hold the process, requirements (photo ID, recent weight), timing, eligibility and refund policy in mind before starting.
working.fix: Split info into just-in-time microcopy at each quiz step instead of upfront prose; measure assessment-start rate and step drop-off.

zeigarnik.evidence: No mention of saving progress or resuming; 'You can pause or cancel at any time' refers to treatment, not the 10-15 minute assessment, so interrupted users have no cue to return.
zeigarnik.fix: Add 'Your progress is saved' and a resume email/SMS link; measure return-to-complete rate.

top.fix: Replace the 16 'Lose 5kg...Lose 80kg' buttons with 3 goal bands (or a slider) and make it step 1 of the quiz.
top.principle: Fewer options reduce decision time and abandonment on mobile.

blocks.label: WeightCare | How it works | Medications | Pricing | ... | Start assessment
How much do you want to lose? 3 bands

top.caption: The 16-option picker collapses to 3 bands inside the main flow, so the user makes one easy choice and meets one CTA.

top.fix: Collapse the 13-link nav into a hamburger with logo, Log in and a single CTA on mobile, and remove 'Learn more' and 'See pricing' from the hero.
top.metric: Primary CTA click-through rate and bounce rate
top.principle: Removing competing stimuli directs attention to the goal action.

blocks.label: 13 nav links incl. Blog, Science, Contact

top.caption: Secondary links move out of the first viewport so the single CTA is the only strong target.

top.fix: Add a 'Step 1 of N' progress bar and start the quiz with the already-selected goal so users begin partway through.
top.principle: Visible progress increases motivation to finish.
top.caption: A progress bar and saved-progress note show how close the finish is and reduce abandonment.

top.fix: Turn the dense 'How it works' paragraph into three numbered steps with a short 'You'll need' checklist (photo ID, recent weight) and a free-assessment note.
top.metric: Scroll depth to CTA and assessment starts
top.principle: Chunked content is scannable and reduces working-memory load on mobile.

blocks.label: Long paragraph: quiz, review, delivery, ID, timing, charges
You'll need: photo ID, recent weight

top.caption: Prose becomes three steps and a checklist, so users see the process and requirements at a glance.

top.fix: Unify CTA copy to one label ('Start free assessment') in one filled style, and style 'Learn more', 'See pricing' and 'View plans' as plain text links.
top.metric: Primary CTA click share and click-through rate
top.principle: Distinct styling for the primary action and consistent styling for secondary ones clarifies hierarchy.
top.caption: One filled CTA style and one label repeated down the page, with secondary actions demoted to text links.

value.summary: The biggest strength is a clear, familiar journey (quiz, clinician review, delivery) with honest reassurance on time (10 to 15 minutes), price (from £149/month) and no charge for the assessment. The biggest weakness is choice and attention overload on mobile: 13 nav links, four near-identical CTAs and 16 'Lose Xkg' options compete with the single goal of starting the assessment.

explain.promise: Ad leads with "Clinician-led weight care. No gimmicks." and "A real prescriber reviews your assessment"; the page H1 is "Take control of your weight" with "Personalised medical weight loss, delivered to your door", so the clinician-led, no-gimmicks promise is absent from the first screen and the tone shifts to generic transformation language.
explain.offer: Ad offers "Start with a free assessment" and "free assessment" in the offer field; the page never says "free" anywhere and only mentions "Cancel anytime", so a cold visitor cannot tell whether the quiz costs anything.
explain.price: Ad shows "plans from £99 a month"; the first and only page price is "From £149/month. Cancel anytime.", which is £50 higher, sits below the fold in the Plans section, and is not shown on the first screen.
explain.proof: Ad cites "Rated Excellent on Trustpilot by 4,000 people"; page replaces it with "Trusted by 50,000+ members" and "Join thousands who have changed their lives", with no Trustpilot rating, no review count and no named reviews, so the ad's specific proof is missing and the substitute is an unsourced headcount.
explain.cta: Ad CTA is "Start free assessment"; page CTAs are "Take the quiz" and "View plans", so the verb "Start" and the word "free" are lost, "quiz" reframes a clinical assessment as a lightweight quiz, and "View plans" competes with the primary action. Its saving grace is that the quiz is a low-commitment step, so it does not ask for more than the ad implied.
explain.visual: No images attached; visual continuity (brand, imagery, Trustpilot badge, clinician presence) could not be judged and would matter for a cold audience.

value.summary: The ad's three hooks (a free assessment, plans from £99 a month and Trustpilot Excellent) are all missing or contradicted on the page, which shows £149/month and 50,000+ members instead. A cold, problem-aware visitor who tapped for a free £99 route sees a higher price and no free offer, so expect bounce and low assessment-start rate, plus compliance exposure on price, free and outcome implications.

gaps.evidence: Ad says "plans from £99 a month"; page says "From £149/month. Cancel anytime." and only below the fold.
gaps.fix: We believe aligning the page price to the ad (or changing the ad to the true entry price of £149) and showing it in the first screen with what is included will reduce price-shock bounce and raise assessment starts; primary metric: assessment start rate (and bounce rate on first screen).

gaps.evidence: Ad says "Start with a free assessment" / "free assessment"; page says nothing about free, only "Cancel anytime".
gaps.fix: We believe adding "Free assessment" with a one-line note of what is free and what happens after (clinician decides, plan price shown) next to the hero CTA will remove cost uncertainty and lift assessment starts; primary metric: assessment start rate.

gaps.evidence: Ad headline "Clinician-led weight care. No gimmicks." and "A real prescriber reviews your assessment"; page H1 "Take control of your weight", with no mention of a prescriber on the first screen.
gaps.fix: We believe changing the H1/subhead to echo the ad ("Clinician-led weight care. A real prescriber reviews your assessment") will cut first-screen bounce from cold Meta traffic; primary metric: first-screen engagement / assessment start rate.

gaps.evidence: Ad says "Rated Excellent on Trustpilot by 4,000 people"; page says "Trusted by 50,000+ members" and "Join thousands who have changed their lives".
gaps.fix: We believe placing the same verifiable Trustpilot rating and review count beside the hero CTA, with a dated source link, in place of or ahead of the unsourced member count will build trust with a cold audience and raise assessment starts; primary metric: assessment start rate.

gaps.evidence: Ad CTA "Start free assessment"; page CTAs "Take the quiz" and "View plans".
gaps.fix: We believe renaming the primary CTA to "Start free assessment" and demoting "View plans" to a secondary text link will keep intent continuous and reduce diversion before the assessment; primary metric: CTA click-through to assessment step 1.

gaps.evidence: Page says "Take the quiz. Our team reviews. Medication delivered." while the ad says a prescriber "builds a plan around your life" and the page FAQ asks "What if I don't qualify?" only at the bottom.
gaps.fix: We believe stating on the first screen that a clinician reviews each assessment and decides whether treatment is appropriate (with the 'What if I don't qualify?' answer surfaced) will set honest expectations, reduce later drop-off at eligibility, and keep claims defensible; primary metric: assessment completion rate.

rules.reason: "Take the quiz. Our team reviews. Medication delivered." presumes the clinical outcome; eligibility and whether medication is prescribed are a clinician's decision and the page should say so near the hero.
Pricing is stated only as "From £149/month" below the fold with no statement of VAT inclusion, what the monthly price covers (consultation, medication) or subscription terms before commitment.
The ad's "free assessment" is not carried onto the page, and the page gives no terms on what happens after the free step (plan price, cancellation), which risks "free" being read as conditional.
"Trusted by 50,000+ members" and "Join thousands who have changed their lives" are objective claims needing substantiation held before publication; "changed their lives" implies an outcome.
"Rated Excellent on Trustpilot by 4,000 people" must match the live Trustpilot rating, review count and period; the figure is unverified here and absent from the page.
"plans from £99 a month" must be available to a reasonable share of buyers and VAT-inclusive; the page shows "From £149/month", suggesting the headline price is not what most visitors will pay.

"Personalised medical weight loss, delivered to your door" and the FAQ "Is it safe?" invite safety and efficacy impressions; the page must not describe treatment as safe or certain to work and should state that results vary and eligibility is clinician-decided.

value.disclosure: Adjacent to the assessment CTA and plan price: that a clinician decides whether any treatment is appropriate and results vary; that the price includes VAT and what it covers; the monthly subscription terms and how to cancel; and what is free (assessment only) versus charged afterwards.

value.summary: The funnel leaks most at Landing page → Quiz start, where only 6.8% of 48,200 users begin the quiz (mobile 6.0% vs desktop 10.0%), and recovering just 10% of those losses is worth roughly £126.5k versus £7.3k for the next-best step. No screenshots were attached, so this is reasoned from the numbers and context only: a 'clinician-led' ad promise with price absent from the ad, a mobile landing page, and a 14-question quiz suggest a mismatch between ad expectation and page (price shock, unclear first step, perceived effort) before users commit. The segment split shows mobile carries 80% of traffic and is weakest at every step, with a notable gap at Quiz complete → Account created (49% vs 68% on desktop), pointing to mobile-specific friction (long quiz, and email, phone and postcode demanded before the result is revealed) on top of the top-of-funnel problem.

hypotheses.hypothesis: We believe that making the quiz CTA visible above the fold on mobile with a clear time and effort promise (e.g. 'Takes 3 minutes, 14 quick questions, clinician-reviewed') and surfacing the starting price near the CTA for mobile users will increase quiz starts because only 6.0% of 38,400 mobile visitors start the quiz versus 10.0% on desktop, and the ad promises clinician-led care but gives no price or effort expectation. We'll know this is true when mobile landing → quiz start rate moves by at least 1.0 percentage point (6.0% to 7.0%) with quiz completion rate and paid conversion rate unchanged.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: Mobile landing page → quiz start rate
hypotheses.guardrail: Quiz completion rate and quiz start → paid conversion rate
hypotheses.surface: Mobile landing page hero and primary CTA
hypotheses.principle: Clarity of next step and expectation setting (reduce uncertainty and perceived effort)
hypotheses.whatToLookAt: Mobile scroll-depth and CTA visibility (heatmaps/session recordings) to see whether users reach the CTA; Meta ad-to-page message match review; bounce and time-on-page by placement (Feed vs Stories/Reels); price-related exit behaviour in recordings; compare against desktop hero layout.

hypotheses.hypothesis: We believe that adding the price (e.g. 'from £X') and the clinician-led proof (clinician credentials and photo) to the Meta ad creative and the matching landing hero for paid social mobile traffic will increase quiz starts among qualified visitors because price appears on the page but not in the ad, so users who click and then hit unexpected price are likely bouncing, and 'clinician-led' is claimed in the ad without visible proof. We'll know this is true when landing → quiz start rate moves by at least 0.8 percentage points (6.8% to 7.6% overall) with ad click-through rate and cost per paid conversion unchanged or better.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: Landing page → quiz start rate (paid social)
hypotheses.guardrail: Cost per paid conversion and ad CTR
hypotheses.surface: Meta ad creative and landing hero message match
hypotheses.principle: Message match and price transparency (set expectations pre-click)
hypotheses.whatToLookAt: CTR vs landing → quiz start by ad variant; bounce rate and time on page for price-in-ad vs not; exit-survey or on-page poll ('what stopped you starting?'); recordings of price-section interactions; qualitative ad comment themes on price.

hypotheses.hypothesis: We believe that replacing the page-length content before the CTA with a short, scannable mobile hero (single-screen value prop, trust badges, first quiz question embedded inline) for mobile visitors will increase quiz starts because 38,400 mobile visitors yield only 2,300 starts and mobile friction (scrolling, load time, tap distance to the CTA) is the likely cause of the 4-point gap to desktop. We'll know this is true when mobile landing → quiz start rate moves by at least 1.2 percentage points (6.0% to 7.2%) with quiz completion rate and page load speed (LCP) unchanged or better.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: Mobile landing page → quiz start rate
hypotheses.guardrail: Quiz completion rate and LCP / bounce rate
hypotheses.surface: Mobile landing page layout and first quiz question
hypotheses.principle: Reduce friction and commitment cost (foot-in-the-door micro-commitment)
hypotheses.whatToLookAt: Mobile page speed (LCP, CLS) from field data; scroll maps and rage-tap data; share of mobile sessions that never scroll to the CTA; in-app browser (Meta webview) vs native browser performance split; click maps on non-interactive elements.

hypotheses.hypothesis: We believe that showing a result teaser (e.g. eligibility or recommended plan) before account creation and deferring phone and postcode to a later step, asking only for email first, for mobile users will increase account creation because mobile completes the account step at 49.2% versus 68.1% on desktop, and requesting email, phone and postcode before revealing the result adds friction and privacy concern after 14 questions. We'll know this is true when mobile quiz complete → account created rate moves by at least 6 percentage points (49.2% to 55.2%) with account → paid conversion rate and data quality (valid phone/postcode rate) unchanged.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: Mobile quiz complete → account created rate
hypotheses.guardrail: Account → paid conversion rate and valid contact data rate
hypotheses.surface: Post-quiz account creation form and result gate
hypotheses.principle: Reciprocity and progressive disclosure (give value before asking for data)
hypotheses.whatToLookAt: Field-level drop-off and error analytics on the account form (email, phone, postcode); mobile keyboard and autofill issues in recordings; form abandonment at phone field specifically; user interviews or poll on why they left before creating an account; compare desktop vs mobile field completion times.

hypotheses.hypothesis: We believe that adding a visible progress indicator, grouping the 14 questions into 3 short sections and enabling single-tap answers with auto-advance on mobile will increase quiz completion because mobile completes at 53.9% versus 70.4% on desktop, suggesting effort and fatigue on small screens rather than lack of intent. We'll know this is true when mobile quiz start → complete rate moves by at least 5 percentage points (53.9% to 58.9%) with answer quality (e.g. skipped/default-answer rate) and account creation rate unchanged.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: Mobile quiz start → quiz complete rate
hypotheses.guardrail: Answer quality (skip/default rate) and quiz complete → account created rate
hypotheses.surface: Mobile quiz UI (progress bar, question layout, tap targets)
hypotheses.principle: Goal-gradient effect and reducing perceived effort
hypotheses.whatToLookAt: Question-by-question drop-off to find the specific questions where users exit; time per question on mobile; sensitive-question exits (medical history, weight, etc.); recordings of mobile quiz sessions for tap-target and scroll problems; consider whether any questions can be cut or made optional.

hypotheses.hypothesis: We believe that testing a lower-commitment entry (a one-question 'Am I a good fit?' tap-through that leads into the full assessment) for cold paid social mobile traffic will increase quiz starts because 93% of landing page visitors do not start, and cold Meta audiences in an interruption context are unlikely to commit to a 14-question assessment without a small first step. We'll know this is true when overall landing → quiz start rate moves by at least 1.0 percentage point (6.8% to 7.8%) with quiz completion rate and paid conversion per landing visitor unchanged or better.
hypotheses.guardrail: Paid conversions per 1,000 landing visitors and quiz completion rate
hypotheses.surface: Landing page CTA and first quiz screen
hypotheses.whatToLookAt: Audience and placement breakdown of start rate (prospecting vs retargeting); new vs returning visitors; intent signals such as time on page and scroll before leaving; review comparable one-question-start benchmarks; check that quiz tracking is firing correctly on mobile webview so the low start rate is not partly a measurement artefact.

language.evidence: Whole page is English: "Take control of your weight", "Start your free assessment". Measured langScore en 7, de 0, only 79 words.
language.fix: Fully translate into German by a native health copywriter, not machine translation. Set lang=de and hreflang, and translate the CTA (e.g. "Kostenlose Einschätzung starten"). Use Sie throughout, and keep medical terms such as Gewichtsreduktion and ärztliche Beratung consistent. Imagery was not visible, so check that any photos and alt text suit a German audience.

price.evidence: "From £149/month. Cancel anytime." Shows £ only, with no € amount, no VAT statement and no shipping reference.
price.fix: Show prices in € in German format (e.g. "ab 149,00 € / Monat inkl. MwSt., zzgl./inkl. Versand") as PAngV requires. State the minimum term and the cancellation terms (Kündigungsfrist) explicitly. Check that "Cancel anytime" is accurate under German consumer law, and replace it with "monatlich kündbar" only if true.

payments.evidence: "Pay by card, Apple Pay or Klarna." Only Klarna is found; PayPal, SEPA-Lastschrift, Rechnung and Giropay/Sofort are missing.
payments.fix: Lead with PayPal, SEPA-Lastschrift and Klarna (including Rechnung), which the provider already supports for PayPal and SEPA. Show the payment logos near the price and CTA, and move cards to a secondary position. Confirm that a recurring subscription can be offered via SEPA mandate.

trust.evidence: "GMC-registered clinician"; "Example Weightcare Ltd, company 12345678, London". No German entity, Impressum, Trusted Shops seal or German phone number is shown.
trust.fix: Replace the GMC claim with "in Deutschland approbierte Ärztinnen und Ärzte". Show the Berlin GmbH with HRB number, USt-IdNr., Geschäftsführer and German address in the footer. Add a +49 30 phone number. Add the Trusted Shops seal only once it is actually active, plus data-protection and security badges.

reviews.evidence: "Rated Excellent on Trustpilot." and "Trusted by 50,000+ members." Trustpilot is the only platform named.
reviews.fix: Use Trusted Shops and Google reviews collected from German customers. Drop the UK-based "50,000+ members" and "Excellent" claims until they can be substantiated for Germany (Abmahnung risk). Make sure no testimonials about prescription medicines appear (HWG §11).

legal.evidence: Footer has only "Privacy" and "Terms". There is no Impressum, Widerrufsbelehrung, Datenschutzerklärung or cookie consent. "Medication delivered next day" and "Personalised medical weight loss" are advertised.
legal.fix: Add an Impressum (TMG/DDG §5) linked on every page, a German Datenschutzerklärung, AGB, a Widerrufsbelehrung with model form, and a consent banner before non-essential cookies. Review all copy with a German HWG lawyer: no advertising of prescription-only weight-loss drugs to consumers, and no promise of outcomes. Frame the offer as a medical consultation and avoid naming drugs. Use compliant wording on the order button ("zahlungspflichtig bestellen") and add the legally required medical-service disclosures.

formats.fix: Use 149,00 €, +49 30 … phone numbers, 24-hour times (8–20 Uhr) and DD.MM.YYYY dates. Give addresses as street then number, then PLZ before city.

delivery.evidence: "Medication delivered next day by Royal Mail."
delivery.fix: Replace with "Versand mit DHL" and a delivery time in Werktage next to the price (e.g. "Lieferung in 1–3 Werktagen"), as long as the pharmacy fulfilment can actually keep that promise. Check that the prescription and pharmacy flow is compliant before promising a delivery time.

support.fix: Provide a German phone number with hours in German format (e.g. "Mo–Fr 8–20 Uhr"), German-language support and a de domain email with a 24-hour reply promise. Add the contact details to the Impressum and the checkout.

culture.evidence: "Take control of your weight" and "Trusted by 50,000+ members" are UK-style emotional claims. The tone is informal and promotional, and there is no Sie form (sie 0, du 0).
culture.fix: Use a sober, factual tone with Sie. Emphasise medical competence, data protection (DSGVO) and transparency over empowerment and social-proof superlatives. Address privacy and the sensitivity of health data early. Avoid overpromising outcomes.

blockers: No Impressum (legal requirement) and no German entity details on the page
No Widerrufsbelehrung, Datenschutzerklärung or cookie consent for a German launch
HWG compliance unchecked: medical weight-loss advertising, no German-licensed clinician wording, and the Trustpilot and member-count claims could attract an Abmahnung
Prices shown only in £ with no inkl. MwSt. or shipping reference (PAngV)
Page is entirely in English with no German-language service or support

hypotheses.hypothesis: We believe that a fully native German page with Sie and a German CTA ("Kostenlose Einschätzung starten") for German health-seeking visitors will increase assessment starts because the page is currently 100% English with de score 0. We'll know this is true when assessment start rate moves by at least 20% relative with bounce rate unchanged.
hypotheses.principle: Native-language clarity reduces cognitive load and builds credibility

value.summary: The page is a direct UK copy: English only, £ pricing, Royal Mail, GMC and Trustpilot, with a London company in the footer and no Impressum, so it cannot launch in Germany as is. Impressum, Widerrufsbelehrung, Datenschutz, cookie consent, PAngV pricing and HWG review are launch blockers, while payment mix, Trusted Shops reviews and tone are optimisations. Once the legal base is in place, test the German-language rewrite, the local entity and trust strip, and the € price with DHL and PayPal/SEPA/Rechnung first, since these map to the biggest gaps; imagery was not visible, so check photos separately.

items.why: The primary metric event is not found in Variant A, so assessment_start cannot be measured for the variant and the test is invalid.
Variant A pushes 'assessment_started' instead of 'assessment_start', so the event name was changed and will not match the primary metric configuration.
The hero inline handler in Variant A pushes the renamed event 'assessment_started'; this is the cause of the broken metric and is out of scope.
data-exp is the same and data-variant differs (control vs A), which is expected for experiment bucketing.
The consent manager is missing in Variant A, creating a compliance risk and a tracking and behaviour difference between arms; not in scope.
The CookieYes script is absent in Variant A, which changes load time and consent behaviour and is out of scope; the GTM script is common to both.

The primary CTA label changed from 'Start your free assessment' to 'Start my assessment', which is within the stated scope; the 'View plans' CTA is unchanged. Note that 'free' was dropped, which is a material offer-wording change.
The data-track attributes are identical (cta_hero, cta_plans) and only the label text differs, so this is a false clash caused by the label change; no tracking loss on the CTAs themselves.
Destinations are identical (/assessment and /pricing); the row is flagged only because of the label text change, so nothing goes somewhere else.
The H1 changed to the clinician-led message as scoped; the H2s are unchanged.
The price changed from £149 to £129/month in Variant A, which is not in scope and would confound conversion results.
The count rose from 47 to 51 words, which is consistent with the H1, subhead and CTA copy changes, though the added copy also includes the price and 'A real prescriber reviews' text.
Variant A adds the Fraunces serif font, a design change outside the copy-only scope.
Variant A loads an extra Fraunces font file from Google Fonts, adding a request and load-time impact and a flash-of-unstyled-text risk; out of scope.
Variant A introduces a new colour (#0b3d3e) that is not in the stated scope of copy-only changes.
The hero image was swapped to /img/hero-clinician.jpg in Variant A, a visual change outside the stated scope that confounds the copy test.
Variant A has one image without alt text (likely the new hero image), an accessibility regression versus control's zero.

blockers: Primary metric event assessment_start is not found in Variant A; it fires as 'assessment_started', so the primary metric cannot be measured and the test is invalid. Restore the exact event name 'assessment_start' in the inline handler and dataLayer push.
Price differs between arms (£149 control vs £129 Variant A); this is out of scope and directly confounds conversion. Revert Variant A to £149.
Consent manager (CookieYes) script is missing in Variant A, which is a compliance risk and a tracking and load-time difference between arms. Restore it.
The hero image was swapped (hero.jpg to hero-clinician.jpg), a visual change outside the copy-only scope that confounds the test. Revert it or formally expand the scope.
Fraunces font, extra Google Fonts request and new colour #0b3d3e were added to Variant A, which is out-of-scope design change and adds load time. Remove them or expand the scope.
warnings: The CTA label drops the word 'free' ('Start your free assessment' to 'Start my assessment'); this is a material offer-wording change that should be explicitly accepted, as it may affect results independently of the clinician-first message.
The new Variant A image has no alt text (1 image without alt vs 0 in control); add alt text.
The subhead copy introduces additional claims ('A real prescriber reviews...') and a price mention; confirm the final wording is the approved scope.
The CookieYes script is absent from Variant A, so analytics consent gating differs between arms, which may skew event counts even once the event name is fixed.
accepted: H1 changed to 'Clinician-led weight care. No gimmicks.'
Subhead copy changed as part of the clinician-first message.
Primary CTA label changed to 'Start my assessment' (destination /assessment and data-track=cta_hero are unchanged).
data-variant marker differs (control vs A) as expected, with data-exp=HERO-14 on both.
value.reason: Variant A fires a renamed event (assessment_started) so the primary metric cannot be measured, and it also changes price, hero image, fonts, colours and the consent manager, none of which are in the copy-only scope.

insights.title: The biggest funnel drop is between hero scroll and CTA click, not inside the quiz
insights.body: 31,300 users scroll past the hero but only 2,890 click the CTA (about 9% of those who scrolled, 6.0% of landing users), versus 2,410 to 1,540 quiz completions after that. Note: the funnel's 3.2% start rate is labelled on the quiz-complete row, so the definition of 'start' should be confirmed.
insights.source: GA4 funnel, last 30 days, mobile paid social

insights.title: 35% of mobile paid social visitors never scroll past the hero
insights.body: 48,200 land and 31,300 scroll past the hero (65%), so roughly 16,900 users see only the hero and never reach the CTA or any reassurance copy.
insights.source: GA4 funnel, last 30 days, mobile paid social

insights.title: A sticky mobile CTA lifted clicks but did not prove a start-rate lift
insights.body: Sticky bar gave +6.1% CTA clicks (p 0.03), but the +3.9% start rate was not significant, so we know it helps clicks and not yet that it helps starts.

insights.title: Putting 'from £149' in the hero reduced CTA clicks, so price needs context, not just prominence
insights.body: The price-on-hero test gave -4.2% CTA clicks but was abandoned at 60% of sample, so the result is directional only and does not show that price disclosure itself is the problem.

insights.title: Swapping the hero image for a lifestyle photo did nothing measurable
insights.body: Result was flat (+0.8%, CI -3% to +4.6%) over 21 days, which suggests imagery is a weak lever compared with clarity about who reviews you and what it costs.

insights.title: Clinician involvement is the top pre-signup question and sits behind a small footer-style line
insights.body: 31% of top pre-signup support questions ask whether a real clinician reviews them, while the page only says 'Our clinicians are registered with the GMC' below the fold.

insights.title: Visitors cannot tell whether a human or a chatbot is behind the assessment
insights.body: P1 said: 'Is this an actual doctor or a chatbot? It doesn't say.' This matches the 31% support theme, but it is one of only 6 sessions.

insights.title: Some visitors hunt for price in the FAQ before they will engage
insights.body: P2 scrolled to the FAQ to find the price first, and P5 asked whether they would have to pay to see the result; price clarity is 24% of support questions too.
insights.source: User testing, 6 sessions, Sept / Support themes, last 60 days

insights.title: 'Will I qualify' anxiety is stopping people before they start
insights.body: P6 wanted to know what happens if she does not qualify before starting, and 18% of support questions ask about qualifying; the FAQ answer is buried rather than near the CTA.
insights.source: User testing, 6 sessions, Sept / Support themes, last 60 days

insights.title: The '50,000+ members' proof point does not read as credible to at least one tester
insights.body: P3 said: '50,000 members means nothing to me, who are they?' Evidence is a single participant, so treat as a hypothesis about testimonial and social proof representativeness.

insights.title: Message match between ads and the hero may be the biggest gap
insights.body: Priya believes top ads lead with 'clinician-led' and 'no gimmicks' while the hero says 'take control'; no ad-to-page conversion data was supplied to confirm this.

es.The ad promises a specific, quantified o: El anuncio promete un resultado específico y cuantificado (hasta un 15% de pérdida de peso) con atención dirigida por clínicos, pero el titular de la página omite la cifra y el enfoque clínico, así que quienes hicieron clic en el anuncio pierden la continuidad y pueden dudar de la afirmación.
es.We believe that rewriting the headline a: Creemos que reescribir el titular y el subtítulo para reflejar la promesa del anuncio (por ejemplo, 'Pierde hasta un 15% de tu peso con atención dirigida por clínicos', más una nota al pie con el resultado calificado) para visitantes de redes sociales de pago y búsqueda aumentará los inicios de evaluación porque el titular actual no traslada el resultado específico ni la afirmación clínica del anuncio. Sabremos que esto es cierto cuando la tasa de inicio de evaluación se mueva al menos un 10% relativo con la tasa de rebote y la tasa de finalización elegible sin cambios.
es.Take control of your weight: Toma el control de tu peso
es.Personalised medical weight loss, delive: Tratamiento médico personalizado para bajar de peso, entregado en tu domicilio
es.Lose up to 15% of your body weight with: Pierde hasta un 15% de tu peso con atención dirigida por clínicos (anuncio)

es.Message match / scent trail: Coincidencia del mensaje / rastro de señal
es.Social proof and credibility claims are: Prueba social y afirmaciones de credibilidad genéricas e inverificables: no hay reseñadores con nombre, ninguna plataforma de reseñas ni calificación, ningún número o enlace de registro en el GMC, ningún clínico nombrado y ninguna mención del regulador de farmacias o prescripción.
es.We believe that replacing generic proof: Creemos que reemplazar la prueba genérica por señales verificables (calificación con estrellas y plataforma nombrada, p. ej. Trustpilot, 2-3 resultados específicos de miembros con consentimiento, un responsable clínico nombrado con un enlace a su número GMC y el registro ante el regulador de farmacias) para visitantes que llegan por primera vez aumentará los inicios de evaluación porque las afirmaciones actuales no tienen fuente y las compras médicas conllevan un alto riesgo percibido. Sabremos que esto es cierto cuando la tasa de inicio de evaluación se mueva al menos un 8% relativo con la tasa de devoluciones y quejas sin cambios.
es.Trusted by 50,000+ members: Con la confianza de más de 50.000 miembros
es.Our clinicians are registered with the G: Nuestros clínicos están registrados en el GMC
es.Specific, verifiable social proof / auth: Prueba social y autoridad específicas y verificables
es.Eligibility and safety uncertainty are b: La incertidumbre sobre elegibilidad y seguridad está enterrada en las preguntas frecuentes, y la página nunca indica el requisito clave (p. ej. el umbral de IMC) ni qué ocurre si el usuario no cumple los requisitos. Los visitantes se enfrentan al cuestionario sin saber si serán aceptados, lo que eleva el esfuerzo percibido y el temor a perder tiempo.
es.We believe that surfacing a short eligib: Creemos que mostrar un resumen breve de elegibilidad (p. ej. criterios de IMC, para quién no es adecuado) y el resultado de 'si no cumples los requisitos' (p. ej. sin cargo) junto al CTA principal para visitantes indecisos que llegan por primera vez aumentará el inicio y la finalización del cuestionario porque las preguntas de elegibilidad están actualmente ocultas en preguntas frecuentes colapsadas. Sabremos que esto es cierto cuando la tasa de inicio del cuestionario se mueva al menos un 8% relativo con la tasa de aprobación del cuestionario sin cambios.
es.Is it safe? Who is eligible? What if I d: ¿Es seguro? ¿Quién es elegible? ¿Qué pasa si no cumplo los requisitos?
es.Reduce anxiety / uncertainty at the poin: Reducir la ansiedad o la incertidumbre en el momento de actuar
es.Pricing is vague and under-contextualise: El precio es vago y carece de contexto. 'Desde £149/mes' no aclara qué está incluido (consulta, medicación, seguimiento), qué nivel de medicación aplica ni si hay cargos adicionales, así que los visitantes no pueden valorar la oferta antes de invertir tiempo en un cuestionario.
es.We believe that adding a transparent pri: Creemos que añadir un bloque de precios transparente (qué incluye, rango de precio por tratamiento, sin cargos ocultos, cancelación en cualquier momento) para visitantes sensibles al precio aumentará la finalización del cuestionario porque el 'Desde £149/mes' aislado deja sin resolver la incertidumbre sobre el coste. Sabremos que esto es cierto cuando la tasa de finalización del cuestionario se mueva al menos un 6% relativo con el abandono del checkout y la tasa de devoluciones sin cambios.
es.Transparency / reduce hidden-cost anxiet: Transparencia / reducir la ansiedad por costes ocultos
es.The headline is a generic, emotive claim: El titular es una afirmación genérica y emotiva que no indica qué es concretamente el servicio (medicación para la pérdida de peso con receta), para quién es ni el resultado cuantificado. La naturaleza medicamentosa solo aparece en la lista de cómo funciona, y 'pérdida de peso médica' resulta ambiguo para los visitantes que llegan por primera vez.
es.We believe that making the value proposi: Creemos que hacer explícita la propuesta de valor en el hero (tratamiento para la pérdida de peso prescrito por un clínico, a quién va dirigido, resultado esperado y plazo) para los visitantes fríos aumentará la profundidad de desplazamiento y el inicio de la evaluación, porque el hero actual obliga a deducir la oferta. Sabremos que es cierto cuando la tasa de inicio de evaluación varíe al menos un 7 % relativo sin cambios en la tasa de rebote.
es.5-second clarity / specificity over slog: Claridad y especificidad en 5 segundos por encima de los eslóganes
es.There is no honest reason to act now: no: No hay una razón honesta para actuar ahora: no se explica el coste de esperar, no hay ninguna señal de capacidad o disponibilidad clínica ni una oferta con plazo. El CTA de cierre 'Únete hoy' es genérico e implica un compromiso en lugar de un siguiente paso de bajo riesgo.
es.We believe that adding a truthful, non-m: Creemos que añadir una razón veraz y no manipuladora para empezar ya (por ejemplo, 'Recibe tu revisión clínica en un plazo de 48 horas' o los tiempos reales de espera actuales para el alta) y alinear el CTA final con 'Empieza tu evaluación gratuita' para los visitantes listos para actuar aumentará los inicios de evaluación, porque la página no ofrece actualmente ninguna motivación basada en el tiempo. Sabremos que es cierto cuando la tasa de inicio de evaluación varíe al menos un 5 % relativo sin cambios en la tasa de reembolsos.
es.Honest urgency / CTA consistency: Urgencia honesta y coherencia del CTA
es.Fuse with research synthesis: Fusionar con la síntesis de investigación
es.Combines the research synthesis (what cu: Combina la síntesis de investigación (lo que dicen y hacen los clientes) con la auditoría de la página (lo que la página hace mal). Un problema que aparece en ambas se fusiona en una sola hipótesis y se marca como corroborado; el resto se conserva etiquetado según su fuente.
es.seen in research and on the page: vistos en la investigación y en la página
es.not visible in the page audit: no visible en la auditoría de la página
es.New visitors from paid and organic traff: Los nuevos visitantes procedentes de tráfico de pago y orgánico no pueden saber cuánto cuesta realmente Juniper, porque la página de destino solo muestra 'Desde 149 £/mes' en la sección de precios, sin aclarar si es por mes o por programa completo, sin mencionar la subida de precio tras la introducción, sin indicar el compromiso total ni afirmar que no hay tarifas adicionales. Esto provoca que se vuelva repetidamente a la sección de precios, consultas sobre el precio en el chat en directo, dudas antes de iniciar la evaluación y cancelaciones en el mes 2 por cargos ocultos percibidos.
es.We believe that replacing the lone 'From: Creemos que sustituir la línea suelta 'Desde 149 £/mes' por un bloque de desglose de precios junto al CTA principal (precio de introducción, precio tras el primer mes, compromiso total, qué incluye y una línea de 'sin otras tarifas') para los nuevos visitantes procedentes de tráfico de pago y orgánico aumentará los inicios de evaluación y reducirá las cancelaciones en el mes 2, porque la investigación muestra a usuarios que vuelven repetidamente a la sección de precios, preguntan en el chat si el precio es definitivo y cancelan tras una subida de precio no advertida, y la auditoría de la página muestra que 'Desde 149 £/mes' no ofrece información sobre lo incluido ni sobre las tarifas. Sabremos que es cierto cuando la tasa de paso de la página de destino a inicio de evaluación aumente al menos un +8 % relativo con la tasa de cancelación a 30 días sin cambios o inferior.
es.Landing page pricing section ('From £149: Sección de precios de la página de destino ('Desde 149 £/mes') y resumen del pago
es.First-time visitors, especially those ag: Primeros visitantes, especialmente los mayores de 35 años, dudan de los resultados y no logran verse reflejados en el programa, porque las pruebas de la página de destino son genéricas e inverificables ('Con la confianza de más de 50 000 miembros', 'Lee nuestras 4 000 reseñas', afirmación sin fuente sobre el GMC sin revisores nombrados, plataforma ni valoración) y los testimonios y las fotos de antes y después parecen falsos y solo muestran a personas de veintitantos años. Esto provoca vacilación o casi abandono antes del registro.
es.We believe that replacing the 'Trusted b: Creemos que sustituir las afirmaciones 'Con la confianza de más de 50 000 miembros' y 'Lee nuestras 4 000 reseñas' y la galería de fotos por pruebas verificables y diversas en edad (valoración en estrellas de una plataforma nombrada, 2-3 historias con consentimiento con iniciales, plazo y aviso de resultados típicos, un responsable clínico nombrado con enlace a su número de colegiado del GMC y registro en el regulador farmacéutico) para los primeros visitantes y los visitantes mayores de 35 años aumentará los inicios de evaluación, porque la investigación muestra a una persona que consideró falsas las fotos y a un encuestado que no pudo identificarse con los testimonios, y la auditoría de la página muestra afirmaciones de prueba sin fuente e inverificables en una compra médica de alto riesgo. Sabremos que es cierto cuando la tasa de inicio de evaluación aumente al menos un +8 % relativo con la tasa de reembolsos y reclamaciones sin cambios.

es.Paid-social and search visitors lose con: Los visitantes de anuncios de pago en redes sociales y búsqueda pierden la continuidad entre el anuncio y la página, porque el anuncio promete un resultado cuantificado (hasta un 15 % de pérdida de peso corporal) con atención dirigida por clínicos, pero el titular de la página de destino elimina tanto la cifra como el enfoque clínico, por lo que quienes hacen clic en el anuncio pueden dudar de la afirmación.
es.Health-cautious visitors and paid-ad arr: Los visitantes cautelosos con su salud y quienes llegan desde anuncios no pueden saber si Juniper es un servicio realmente clínico y seguro, porque la página de destino oculta '¿Es seguro? ¿Quién es elegible? ¿Y si no me cualifico?' en preguntas frecuentes plegadas, no ofrece nombres de clínicos ni enlace al GMC y no explica la participación del médico de cabecera, los efectos secundarios ni qué ocurre después del cuestionario. El anuncio promete contacto clínico que no se produce en la primera semana, lo que provoca dudas antes de empezar y decepción después.

es.Start with the mobile hero fix, which ha:

es.None of these three experiments has prod: Ninguno de estos tres experimentos ha producido una victoria: los 3 de 3 resultaron planos, todos en la superficie de evaluación. El principio "set expectations" se ha probado 2 veces y resultó plano en ambas, una con visitantes de paid social y otra con todos los visitantes, mientras que "progressive disclosure" se ha probado una vez, en móvil, y también resultó plano, con una inclinación de +9,1 % cuyo intervalo incluye el cero. No se ha probado nada en ninguna superficie distinta de la evaluación, y los únicos segmentos cubiertos son paid social, móvil y todos los visitantes, así que no hay victorias en ningún segmento, superficie o principio. El mayor hueco es que todos los tests hasta ahora se sitúan en una sola superficie, lo que deja el resto del embudo, y cualquier segmento distinto de paid social y móvil, completamente sin examinar.

es.\"Guaranteed\", \"always\", \"never fail: «Garantizado», «siempre», «nunca falla», «sin riesgo», «100 %» prometen un resultado que la empresa no puede asegurar. Solo se permiten cuando exista una garantía contractual y se indiquen sus condiciones.
es.\"Free\" is only acceptable when the con: «Gratis» solo es aceptable cuando el consumidor no paga nada más que los gastos inevitables de envío o de respuesta y no existe ninguna condición oculta; la «prueba gratuita» necesita junto a ella el precio posterior a la prueba y las condiciones de cancelación.
es.UK DMCC Act 2024 (in force April 2025) a: La Ley DMCC del Reino Unido de 2024 (en vigor desde abril de 2025) y la lista negra de la Directiva UCPD de la UE prohíben las declaraciones falsas de que una oferta tiene plazo limitado o de que las existencias son escasas. Los contadores atrás y los mensajes del tipo «solo quedan 3» deben ser ciertos y verificables; la FTC estadounidense considera engañoso lo mismo.
es.Testimonials and endorsements must be ge: Los testimonios y respaldos deben ser auténticos y estar declarados.
es.Reviews and testimonials must be real, c: Las reseñas y testimonios deben ser reales, actuales y típicos, o ir acompañados de resultados típicos, y debe declararse cualquier pago o vínculo material (Directrices de la FTC sobre respaldos de 2023; CAP del Reino Unido 3.45–3.50; prohibición de reseñas falsas de la UCPD de la UE de 2022). No se permiten personas inventadas ni reseñas pagadas presentadas como orgánicas.
Las indicaciones de precio deben ser completas.
es.Headline prices must include unavoidable: Los precios destacados deben incluir las tasas inevitables y los impuestos para el público destinatario (con IVA incluido para consumidores del Reino Unido y la UE; norma de la FTC de 2025 sobre cargos ocultos para eventos en directo y alojamiento, y legislación estatal de California); los precios «desde» deben estar disponibles para una parte razonable de los compradores, y las condiciones de suscripción deben ser claras antes del compromiso.
Sin patrones oscuros en la llamada a la acción.
es.Pre-ticked consent, confirm-shaming (\"N: Las casillas preseleccionadas, el acoso por culpabilización («No, no quiero ahorrar dinero»), la cancelación oculta y la insistencia están prohibidos o son objeto de sanción según la Ley DMCC del Reino Unido, el artículo 25 de la Ley de Servicios Digitales de la UE y la FTC. Las llamadas a la acción deben indicar qué ocurrirá después.
Claro, justo y no engañoso en conjunto.
es.The impression a reasonable consumer tak: Se juzga la impresión que se forma un consumidor razonable con el anuncio completo, incluidas las omisiones. Los beneficios sin condiciones materiales, o un beneficio destacado con una matización escondida, incumplen aunque cada frase sea literalmente cierta.
es.\"Your data is safe/secure\", \"GDPR-com: «Sus datos están seguros», «cumple el RGPD», «impulsado por IA», «imparcial» son afirmaciones. La FTC actúa contra el «AI-washing» (2024); la Ley de IA de la UE exige transparencia cuando las personas interactúan con una IA o ven contenido generado por IA. Diga lo que sea realmente cierto y verificable.

es.Step conversion = users at this step ÷ u: Conversión por paso = usuarios en este paso ÷ usuarios en el paso anterior. Valor de una fuga = las conversiones finales adicionales que obtendrías si recuperaras el 10% de los usuarios perdidos en ese paso (continúan con las tasas de los pasos posteriores del embudo), multiplicado por el valor por conversión. Ordenar por usuarios recuperables, y no por tasa del paso, evita que un paso final pequeño parezca más grave que un inicio enorme. Todo se calcula en la página; la IA solo interpreta.

es.The funnel leaks most at Landing page →: El embudo pierde más en Página de aterrizaje → Inicio del test, donde solo el 6,8% de 48.200 usuarios empieza el test (móvil 6,0% frente a escritorio 10,0%), y recuperar solo el 10% de esas pérdidas vale unas 126,5 mil £ frente a 7,3 mil £ del siguiente mejor paso. es.Cap nav to 4 items and weight choices to: Limita la navegación a 4 elementos y las opciones de peso a 3-5 rangos; mide el tiempo hasta el primer clic y la tasa de inicio de la evaluación.

es.Split info into just-in-time microcopy a: Divide la información en microcopy en el momento justo en cada paso del cuestionario, en lugar de prosa al inicio; mide la tasa de inicio de la evaluación y el abandono por paso.
es.Productivity soars when a computer and i: La productividad se dispara cuando un ordenador y sus usuarios interactúan a un ritmo (<400 ms) que garantiza que ninguno tenga que esperar.
es.Response timing cannot be judged from st: El tiempo de respuesta no puede evaluarse a partir de contenido estático; solo son visibles 9 scripts y 3 KB de HTML, sin evidencia de latencia.
es.Instrument INP and step-transition time: Mide el INP y el tiempo de transición entre pasos al hacer clic en 'Continuar', y prueba si una transición inferior a 400 ms mejora la tasa de finalización de los pasos del cuestionario.
es.The time to acquire a target is a functi: El tiempo para alcanzar un objetivo es función de la distancia hasta él y de su tamaño.
es.No screenshots attached; judged from str: No se adjuntaron capturas de pantalla; se juzga solo por la estructura. es.Make the hero CTA full-width with at lea: Haz que el CTA del hero ocupe todo el ancho, con al menos 48 px de altura y fijo en la parte inferior en móvil; mide la tasa de toques erróneos y el clic en el CTA.
es.The mental state of being fully immersed: Estado mental de inmersión total en una actividad, con una concentración energizada.
es.The path 'Start your free assessment' ->: El recorrido 'Empieza tu evaluación gratuita' -> objetivo de peso -> 'Continuar' es sencillo, pero los CTA 'Más información' y 'Ver precios' y un formulario de 8 campos interrumpen el impulso con salidas.

es.Users never read manuals but start using: Los usuarios nunca leen los manuales, pero empiezan a usar el software de inmediato.
es.Users will tap straight into the quiz, b: Los usuarios entrarán directamente al cuestionario, pero la sección de cómo funciona es un párrafo largo que los usuarios de móvil se saltarán, dejando enterrados requisitos como 'documento de identidad con foto y un peso reciente'.
es.Surface the 'You'll need: photo ID and r: Muestra 'Necesitarás: documento de identidad con foto y peso reciente' en una lista breve justo antes del CTA; mide el abandono a mitad de la evaluación.
es.Be liberal in what you accept, and conse: Sé liberal en lo que aceptas y conservador en lo que envías.
es.The form has 8 fields and requires 'phot: El formulario tiene 8 campos y requiere 'documento de identidad con foto y un peso reciente', pero la página no menciona ninguna entrada flexible (unidades kg/st, alternativas de subida de archivos).
es.Accept kg, st/lb and cm/ft-in with auto-: Acepta kg, st/lb y cm/ft-in con conversión automática y permite subir el documento de identidad más adelante; mide la tasa de error en los campos y la finalización del formulario.

es.The tendency to approach a goal increase: La tendencia a acercarse a una meta aumenta a medida que se está más cerca de ella.
es.There is no progress indicator or sense: No hay indicador de progreso ni sensación de avance; el texto menciona una evaluación de 10 a 15 minutos pero no muestra pasos, y 'Continuar' no transmite cuántos pasos quedan.
es.Add a 'Step 1 of 5' progress bar with pr: Añade una barra de progreso 'Paso 1 de 5' con el primer paso prerrellenado (objetivo seleccionado) y mide la tasa de finalización de la evaluación.
es.Any task will inflate until all of the a: Cualquier tarea se expandirá hasta ocupar todo el tiempo disponible.
es.The page sets a time expectation: 'Most: La página fija una expectativa de tiempo: 'La mayoría completa la evaluación en 10 a 15 minutos y recibe respuesta en un plazo de 24 horas'.
es.Move the '10-15 minutes' time promise on: Traslada la promesa de '10-15 minutos' al CTA como microcopy y prueba el tiempo y la tasa de finalización.

es.People judge an experience largely by ho: Las personas juzgan una experiencia sobre todo por cómo se sintieron en su punto álgido y al final.
es.The end of the page is FAQs and footer l: El final de la página son las preguntas frecuentes y los enlaces del pie (Privacidad, Términos, Contacto) en lugar de un CTA final, y 'Si no cumples los requisitos, te explicaremos por qué' sugiere un estado final negativo sin ningún suavizante descrito.
